statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-96225 (GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App, System.Private.CoreLib): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so at its own .NET version. The seven System.Private.CoreLib.dll copies per build and architecture are in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and, in dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, in the .NET SDK's shared framework, the runtime pack and NativeAOT runtime pack (each as a nupkg, and the NativeAOT pack also installed in the SDK) and the .NET and ASP.NET Core runtime archives; the five libcoreclr.so files are in the same two shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the two runtime archives. No copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on (for example, System.Private.CoreLib.dll and libcoreclr.so carry version 10.0.1026.32716 in 10.0.10-r0 and 10.0.1326.50504 in 10.0.13-r0 on both architectures). The fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481 on release/10.0.1xx ("Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions"), which changes the shared-memory and named-mutex code compiled into libcoreclr.so and the Unix Mutex code in System.Private.CoreLib; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112 (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481). Every libcoreclr.so and System.Private.CoreLib.dll records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from, and on both architectures that is the v10.0.110 tag in 10.0.10-r0 and the v10.0.113 tag in 10.0.13-r0. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96225 (GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App, System.Private.CoreLib): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists Linux and macOS as the affected platforms and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32, and the .NET 8.0.32 release notes list this CVE (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). Between the dotnet/runtime v8.0.31 and v8.0.32 tags, the shared-mutex code in the CoreCLR platform layer (sharedmemory.cpp and mutex.cpp) changes in 'Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions', which stops changing permissions on globally visible directories and stops following symbolic links when it validates and fixes them (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/3928fdb88d27fbbd7591f558bcf90b12624944a4, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/compare/v8.0.31...v8.0.32). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. Per build and architecture there are four System.Private.CoreLib.dll files, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap and in the runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and four libcoreclr.so files, in the same two shared frameworks, the runtime pack and the Crossgen2 pack; the runtime pack directory inside that SDK links to the SDK's shared-framework copies. Every one of these files carries the build's own .NET version, and no copy from another .NET version is present. libcoreclr.so names the dotnet/runtime commit it was built from: v8.0.31 (1219a42122cf) in 8.0.31-r0 and v8.0.32 (b9a49e4a6d3a), which contains the shared-mutex change, in 8.0.32-r0; the earlier builds carry 8.0.23 to 8.0.29 and the later builds 8.0.33 and 8.0.34. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

Microsoft lists the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md. The .NET 10 fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481 on release/10.0.1xx ("Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions"), which changes the CoreCLR PAL shared-memory and named-mutex code and the Unix Mutex code in System.Private.CoreLib, outside tests; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one System.Private.CoreLib.dll and one libcoreclr.so, both in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>, and one singlefilehost in the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Host pack, the host that single-file apps are published with. A strings search of every ELF file in 10.0.402-0 for amd64 finds the runtime's shared-memory markers (SharedMemoryException and lockfiles) in libcoreclr.so and singlefilehost, and also in libclrjit.so and libmscordaccore.so in the same shared framework directory, and in no other ELF file. No other copy of any of these files is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The version of all of them is 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, the same on both architectures (for example, 10.0.1226.42308 in 10.0.401-1 and 10.0.1326.50504 in 10.0.402-0). Every copy records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

The .NET 10 fix is dotnet/dotnet commit 46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481 on release/10.0.1xx ("Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions"), which changes the CoreCLR PAL shared-memory and named-mutex code and the Unix Mutex code in System.Private.CoreLib, outside tests; it is in the v10.0.113 source tag and not in v10.0.112: https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/46e12b57000895ce6d079112888fdc3e68198481. DHI dotnet-sdk-10 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 10 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source in the DHI Debian repository, 10.0.301-0, 10.0.302-0, 10.0.302-1, 10.0.400-1, 10.0.401-0, 10.0.401-1, 10.0.402-0, 10.0.403-0, 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-10 and dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-10-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-10 build carries one System.Private.CoreLib.dll and one libcoreclr.so, both in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>, and one singlefilehost in the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Host pack, the host that single-file apps are published with. A strings search of every ELF file in 10.0.402-0 for amd64 finds the runtime's shared-memory markers (SharedMemoryException and lockfiles) in libcoreclr.so and singlefilehost, and also in libclrjit.so and libmscordaccore.so in the same shared framework directory, and in no other ELF file. No other copy of any of these files is present, including inside the nupkg archives. The version of all of them is 10.0.9 in 10.0.301-0, 10.0.10 in 10.0.302-0 and 10.0.302-1, 10.0.11 in 10.0.400-1, 10.0.12 in 10.0.401-0 and 10.0.401-1, 10.0.13 in 10.0.402-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.403-0 and 10.0.15 in 10.0.404-0 and 10.0.404-1, the same on both architectures (for example, 10.0.1226.42308 in 10.0.401-1 and 10.0.1326.50504 in 10.0.402-0). Every copy records the dotnet/dotnet commit it was built from: the v10.0.109 to v10.0.112 tags in the builds up to 10.0.401-1, and the v10.0.113, v10.0.114 and v10.0.115 tags from 10.0.402-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 10.0.402-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96225 (GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2) is a .NET elevation of privilege issue in the runtime (Microsoft.NETCore.App): on Unix, the named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symbolic-link races and unsafe permission changes, so a local attacker can truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions or elevate privileges. Microsoft lists the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w6wh-p4g7-mpj2, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/476, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135706, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md. The .NET 8 fix is dotnet/runtime commit 3928fdb88d27fbbd7591f558bcf90b12624944a4 on release/8.0 ("Fixes for Shared Mutex privileges/permissions"), which changes the CoreCLR PAL shared-memory and named-mutex code; it is in the v8.0.32 tag and not in v8.0.31: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/3928fdb88d27fbbd7591f558bcf90b12624944a4. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 packages Microsoft's .NET 8 SDK for Linux, which includes the .NET runtime and the ASP.NET Core shared framework. We scanned every package built from this source that the DHI Debian repository had published by 2026-11-27, 8.0.422-0, 8.0.423-0, 8.0.423-1, 8.0.424-1, 8.0.425-0, 8.0.425-1, 8.0.426-0, 8.0.427-0, 8.0.428-0 and 8.0.428-1, for amd64 and arm64 (the dotnet-sdk-8 and dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published), after verifying each against its index checksum and including the files inside the nupkg archives they hold. The dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Every dotnet-sdk-8 build carries one System.Private.CoreLib.dll, in the .NET runtime shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>. The PAL code the fix changes is compiled into native ELF files, so we searched the strings of all 19 ELF files in each build, including those inside the nupkg archives (none are), for the PAL's SharedMemoryException marker. It appears in four files in every build: libcoreclr.so, libclrjit.so and libmscordaccore.so in that shared framework directory, and singlefilehost in the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Host pack, the host that single-file apps are published with. The other 15 ELF files, including createdump and libmscordbi.so, do not contain it. The version of the runtime files is 8.0.28 in 8.0.422-0, 8.0.29 in 8.0.423-0 and 8.0.423-1, 8.0.30 in 8.0.424-1, 8.0.31 in 8.0.425-0 and 8.0.425-1, 8.0.32 in 8.0.426-0, 8.0.33 in 8.0.427-0 and 8.0.34 in 8.0.428-0 and 8.0.428-1, the same on both architectures (for example, 8.0.3126.42015 in 8.0.425-1 and 8.0.3226.50405 in 8.0.426-0). Every one of these files records the dotnet/runtime commit it was built from: the v8.0.28 to v8.0.31 tags in the builds up to 8.0.425-1, and the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tags from 8.0.426-0 on, all three of which contain the fix commit. The range ends at 8.0.426-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
